observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: Three independent observations. (1) The body ends in the single instruction RET 8 at 0x0063577f, so the callee pops two four-byte words. semantic_contract: Show or hide a UTFWin window identified by its control id. Invariants, in the order the body establishes them: (1) the receiver arrives in ECX and is the object whose +0x14 pointer vector 0x00634dc0 scans; it is used for exactly one thing, the lookup, and is then abandoned; (2) the first argument is a 32-bit UTFWin control id; (3) the lookup searches every registered root in order, and for each root compares the root's own GetControlID() first and then asks the root for FindWindowByID(id, true), stopping at the first hit; (4) if the lookup yields null, the function performs no virtual call, no memory write and no global access, and returns immediately after popping its two arguments; (5) if the lookup yields a window, the function tail-transfers to the window's vtable slot +0x7C with the receiver in ECX, the constant 1 as the first argument and the caller's second argument as the second, so the only state it can change is that window's kWinFlagVisible flag; (6) the function never reads or writes a global, never allocates, never loops, and has no return value; (7) because the transfer is a tail call, the +0x7C target must use RET 8, and the caller's two argument words are consumed by whichever path is taken.
classification_rationale: The complete body, ABI, argument roles, the single constant, the branch polarity, the tail-transfer mechanics and the virtual slot offset are read directly from the disassembly, and the callee's search algorithm is read from its own disassembly. The virtual slot is identified as UTFWin::IWindow::SetFlag with multi-site corroboration but not from a located vtable, because this binary has no MSVC RTTI and the receiver's dynamic type was never observed. Two material elements are therefore bounded rather than established: the class that owns the +0x14 registry vector, and the concrete IWindow subclass that the +0x7C dispatch reaches at runtime. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld for those two bounds; STRUCTURAL_ONLY is not applicable because the behavioural claim is supported by the body, the inlined sibling evidence and the caller argument patterns, not by structure alone.
semantic_findings: The function is a UTFWin visibility setter keyed by control id: it resolves the id to a window and writes kWinFlagVisible with the caller's boolean.

The flag is hard-coded to 1. Every recorded callsite passes either 0 or 1 as the second argument, and 0x006358c0 contains the inlined pair SetFlag(1,1) and SetFlag(1,0), so the only reachable behaviour is show/hide.

Resolution is a registry scan, not a tree walk from a single root: 0x00634dc0 iterates every element of the receiver's +0x14 vector and searches each element's window hierarchy, which explains the very high fan-in of 27 callers spread over the Editor, UTFWin, Palettes, Sporepedia and ArgScript regions.
Failure is silent and side-effect free. The null path is a single RET 8 and no caller tests a result, so a stale control id simply does nothing.

The dispatch is a tail call, so the callee inherits the caller's frame. This is observable in the reconstruction: the +0x7C target must pop 8 bytes, and the reconstruction's model test exercises exactly that.

The receiver is genuinely consumed: ECX is forwarded unchanged into 0x00634dc0, which immediately does ADD ECX,0x14. This is what rules out a free function and establishes a sibling method on the registry class.
unresolved_questions: Which class owns the +0x14 registry vector? The vector's element type and the meaning of its slot +0x0C (a get-object-by-type query) are not established, and no vtable for the receiver was located.

What is the dynamic IWindow subclass of the resolved window, and therefore which concrete SetFlag implementation runs? No receiver was observed at a dispatch site, and no original-process trace exists.
Is the vector at +0x14 a list of UTFWin service providers, a list of root windows, or a type registry? The observed protocol (query by type id, then treat the result as a window) fits all three.

The control ids pushed by callers are addresses of string literals in .rdata (0x00406678, 0x004066b8, 0x0044 6a98 and so on). Their character contents were not read, so no caller-level purpose is claimed for any individual window.

Spore-ModAPI declares Editors::PlayModeUI::SetWindowVisible at 0x635450/0x635750, numerically adjacent to this target. Whether this target is that method could not be confirmed: 0x00635750 is not a function boundary in this image and 0x00634dc0 does not match PlayModeUI::FindWindowByID's described shape. Recorded as a candidate, not a claim.

Why do all 27 callers load ECX from a field and then call a function that would work equally well as a free function? The most likely reading is a source-level member call whose receiver happens to be unused on the fast path, but that is INFERRED, not observed.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has ever been captured for this function; the original Cell stage has never been entered in any recorded run. Every claim here is static.

A runtime differential test would have to (a) confirm the lookup returns the same window for a given control id, (b) confirm the +0x7C dispatch reaches an IWindow::SetFlag implementation and not a patched one, and (c) confirm the callee really uses RET 8, which the tail transfer requires but which no in-binary observation of the concrete callee can prove.

body_reconstruction.claim_scope: The 34-byte body is reproduced instruction for instruction as a naked function, the vtable layout of the dispatched interface is declared with asserted offsets, the callee is kept as an explicitly named opaque port with its observed contract documented, and the receiver type is declared opaque with only the +0x14 vector asserted. No class is claimed for the receiver and no concrete callee is claimed for the +0x7C slot.
body_reconstruction.byte_exactness: Verified by objdump against the live bytes: the eleven instructions and the RET 8 immediate match exactly. The only difference is the relative displacement of the single CALL, because the reconstruction calls a locally named opaque port rather than 0x00634dc0.
body_reconstruction.host_abi_note: clang's i386 Linux __thiscall models the callee stack pop but not the ECX receiver, so a C++ caller of a __thiscall function is unreliable on this host. UtfWin_00635760_host_bridge is therefore a host shim, not part of the original body: it rebuilds the original __thiscall frame (receiver into ECX, the two arguments on the stack, the caller's return address on top) and transfers control into the byte-exact body. All C++ declarations in the header are plain cdecl and the original convention is recorded in comments and in observed_original_abi.
